info.title: DPOLens
info.summary: Policies and law, with citations a client can check
info.description:
The only way into DPOLens. Every surface, including the MCP server and the
dashboard, is a client of this API.

Interfaces change without notice until 1.0. Errors are
[RFC 9457](https://www.rfc-editor.org/info/rfc9457/) problem details, and `type`
is the field to branch on.

post.summary: Say a new clause is the same rule as a clause of the version before
post.description: For a clause the draft has as new, and a clause of the version before that nothing in the draft continues: the clause continues it, renumbered, reworded or both, as a match made when the draft was uploaded would, so that a citation of that clause says where its rule is now. The flag on the clause is settled by it, and `POST /draft/matches/{key}/reject` undoes it.

post.summary: Say a clause is a different rule from the one it was matched to or asked about
post.description: A matched clause becomes new, and the clause of the version before that it was matched to becomes removed, so that a citation of that clause says its rule was removed. For a new clause whose flag asks whether it is the same rule as a clause of the version before, the answer is no, and the clause stays new. The flag on the clause is settled by it, and the pair is never matched or asked about again.

post.summary: Fix how a clause was read, without changing a word
post.description: Split a clause where a second rule begins, merge it with the clause before it, make a heading text or text a heading, or move it under the clause before it or out a level. Keys follow from where each clause ends up, by the rules a parse uses, and each clause the fix moved or reshaped takes the layer `reviewer`. An open flag on the clause is resolved by the fix. The numbering checks run again, so a numbering flag the fix makes untrue is resolved and a new finding is a new flag; for a new version, the clauses the fix rewords are matched again.
